businessModel: Opt-in privacy ads (BAT), Brave Search ads/API, Brave VPN, Leo and Search Premium subscriptions; Brave Origin one-time purchase
paidNote: Brave Origin $59.99 one-time (Linux free); Brave VPN, Leo Premium and other subscriptions optional
updateCadence: Roughly every 2-4 weeks on the Chromium cycle, with point releases between
summary: Chromium-based browser with Shields blocking, fingerprint farbling, Tor windows, sync chain, and optional Leo AI, Rewards and VPN. Brave Origin (2026) is a paid stripped-down edition.
bestFor: People who want blocking and privacy with zero setup
Chrome users who want to keep Chromium compatibility
Users who want to keep uBO-style MV2 blockers on a Chromium engine
Users who want a Chromium browser without Google services
notFor: People who dislike crypto, AI and promo extras (unless they buy Origin)
Users who want a non-Chromium engine

pros.title: Blocking by default
pros.detail: Shields blocks ads, trackers, third-party cookie tracking and upgrades HTTPS with no setup.

pros.title: Fingerprint farbling
pros.detail: Randomises fingerprint surfaces per session and eTLD+1 rather than a single fixed value.

pros.title: Chromium compatibility
pros.detail: Chrome Web Store extensions and near-perfect site compatibility.

pros.title: Partial MV2 survival
pros.detail: Keeps self-hosted MV2 builds of uBO, AdGuard, uMatrix and NoScript working after Chrome removed MV2.

pros.title: E2EE sync chain
pros.detail: Sync needs no account, just a sync code, and is end-to-end encrypted.

pros.title: Fast Chromium patching
pros.detail: Ships Chromium security point releases within days (1.97.57 and 1.97.59 in Oct 2026).

cons.title: Bundled extras
cons.detail: Rewards, Wallet, VPN upsells, News and Leo are present unless you disable them or pay for Origin.

cons.title: Past controversies
cons.detail: Affiliate-link injection (2020) and the crypto-ads model reduced trust for some users.

cons.title: Mobile extension gap
cons.detail: Android extension support is still experimental behind a flag; iOS has none.

cons.title: Chromium monoculture
cons.detail: Same engine as Chrome and Edge, so engine diversity is not improved.

faq.q: Is Brave still usable with uBlock Origin?
faq.a: Partly: Brave keeps self-hosted MV2 builds of uBO, AdGuard, uMatrix and NoScript working, but the Chrome Web Store no longer lists MV2 extensions. Its built-in Shields covers most blocking needs anyway.
A 2026 paid edition ($59.99 one-time, 10 devices, Linux free) that removes Rewards, Wallet, VPN promos, Leo, News and sponsored images while keeping Shields.

faq.q: Does Brave support extensions on Android?
faq.a: Not yet for normal users; work started in Sept-Oct 2026 behind brave://flags/#brave-android-extensions, Canary first.
